title: Lecture 2 — Applications
description: Apply HTML document, accessibility, text, list, entity, semantic, and link concepts to coding scenarios.
subject: Web Development

questions.question: You are starting a brand new HTML5 document. After writing the DTD, what is the best way to write your opening HTML tag to indicate the document is in English?
questions.explanation: The html element's lang attribute identifies the document language using a language tag such as en.

questions.question: A screen reader is navigating your web page. To help the user understand the hierarchical structure of your content, you should:
options: Use heading tags (<h1>, <h2>, etc.) in proper numerical order.

Put all text inside a single

tag.
Avoid using headings and use list items instead.
questions.correctAnswer: Use heading tags (<h1>, <h2>, etc.) in proper numerical order.
questions.explanation: A meaningful heading hierarchy helps screen-reader users navigate and understand page structure.

questions.question: You want to center a paragraph of text on your web page. Which code is correct based on Chapter 2?
questions.explanation: The supplied lecture answer key identifies the paragraph align attribute for this example.

questions.question: You want to apply strong importance to a word in your paragraph, causing it to stand out, usually in bold. Which phrase element should you use?
questions.explanation: The strong element conveys strong importance, commonly rendered in bold.

questions.question: Which example shows proper HTML nesting?
questions.explanation: Nested elements must close in the reverse order in which they were opened.

questions.question: You are creating an ordered list and want uppercase letters (A, B, C) instead of numbers. How should you format the opening tag?
questions.explanation: The ordered list type attribute can select uppercase alphabetic markers.

questions.question: You have a Top 10 list and want the list markers to count backward. Which HTML attribute should you use?
questions.explanation: The reversed attribute makes an ordered list count down.

questions.question: You need to create a list of grocery items with bullets. Which tag combination will you use?
questions.explanation: An unordered list uses ul for the list and li for each item.

questions.question: You are building an FAQ page. A question is followed by its indented answer. Which list structure is best suited for this?
questions.explanation: A description list pairs terms or questions with their descriptions or answers.

questions.question: You want to display the phrase "HTML & CSS" on your web page. Which entity code should you use for the ampersand?
questions.explanation: The & character reference represents an ampersand in HTML.

questions.question: You are structuring a blog post. Which HTML5 semantic tag is best suited to wrap the core content of the page?
questions.explanation: The main element identifies the primary content of the document.

questions.question: You want to place a copyright notice and contact information at the very bottom of your web page. Which structural element is designed for this?
questions.explanation: The footer element represents footer content for a page or section.

questions.question: You want to create a hyperlink to the Yahoo website. Which is a correct absolute hyperlink?
questions.explanation: An absolute hyperlink uses an anchor element with an href containing the destination URL.

questions.question: You are editing index.html and want to link to contact.html in the same folder. Which is the correct relative hyperlink?
questions.explanation: A relative link names a resource relative to the current page and uses the anchor href attribute.

questions.question: You want to add an email link for help@mysite.com. Which URL scheme must you use in the href attribute?
questions.explanation: The mailto scheme creates a link that opens an email client addressed to the specified recipient.

questions.question: A developer uses <meta charset="utf-8">. What specific problem does this solve?
options: It ensures the website loads quickly on mobile devices.
It provides instructions to the server on how to compress images.
It ensures the internal representation of letters, numbers, and symbols is interpreted correctly by the browser.
It links the HTML document to a CSS stylesheet.
questions.correctAnswer: It ensures the internal representation of letters, numbers, and symbols is interpreted correctly by the browser.
questions.explanation: The charset metadata tells the browser which character encoding to use when interpreting the document.

questions.question: You want to leave a reminder in your HTML code that visitors should not see. What should you type?
questions.explanation: HTML comments are for source notes and are not rendered as page content.

questions.question: Which tag would you use to define a definition for a specific word, usually displayed in italics according to standard conventions?
questions.explanation: The dfn element marks the defining instance of a term.

questions.question: You want to force a line break inside a paragraph, but your editor flags an error because you typed </br>. What is the correct HTML line break tag?
questions.explanation: The br element is a void element and is written without a closing tag.

questions.question: You run your page through the W3C validator and receive an error regarding your heading tags. What is the most likely cause based on good coding practices?
options: You used an <h1> tag inside the <head> section instead of the <body>.
You styled a heading using CSS.
You used an <h1> tag in the body section.
Headings are no longer supported in HTML5.
questions.correctAnswer: You used an <h1> tag inside the <head> section instead of the <body>.
questions.explanation: Heading content belongs in the body, not the document head.
